title: Grammar: simple present, active and passive
competency: Describe daily routines in the simple present tense, in the active and passive voice.

keywords.def: The verb form for habits, routines and facts: "Cows give milk."
A sentence where the doer is the subject: "Farmers sell crops."
A sentence where the thing acted on is the subject, with am/is/are + past participle: "Crops are sold by farmers."

en.text: Use the simple present for routines and facts: "Farmers sell crops." In the active voice, the doer comes first. In the passive voice, the thing acted on comes first and the verb is am/is/are + past participle: "Crops are sold by farmers." Put the doer after "by", or leave it out when it is not important. Use "is" with a singular subject and "are" with a plural subject.

am.text: የአሁን ቀላል ጊዜ ልማዶችንና እውነታዎችን ይገልጻል። በገቢር ሠሪው ይቀድማል፤ በተገብሮ ደግሞ am/is/are + past participle ይመጣል፤ "Crops are sold by farmers."

screens.title: Two ways to say it
screens.ask: "Farmers sell crops." and "Crops are sold by farmers." What is different?
opts: Which word comes first and the verb form
screens.after: Same meaning. In the second, "crops" comes first and the verb is "are sold" (passive).

screens.title: Active and passive
paras: Active: doer + verb (+s) + object. "Cows give milk." "My uncle sows soybean every year."
Passive: object + am/is/are + past participle (+ by doer). "Milk is given by cows." "Soybean is sown every year by my uncle."
Singular subject → is: "A horse is ridden by me."  Plural subject → are: "Beehives are kept by farmers."
The doer can be left out: "Spices are sown in between the onions and peppers."

screens.title: Key words
defs: The verb form for habits, routines and facts: "Cows give milk."
A sentence where the doer is the subject: "Farmers sell crops."
A sentence where the thing acted on is the subject, with am/is/are + past participle: "Crops are sold by farmers."

items: Daily labourers earn the smallest income.
Seeds are sown on time by farmers.
screens.why: Passive sentences have am/is/are + past participle.
screens.clue: Look for is/are + a past participle.

screens.ask: Make it passive: "Farmers sell crops and cereals." → "Crops and cereals ___ by farmers."
Make it passive: "Cows give milk." → "Milk ___ by cows."

screens.text: Choose the correct passive: "My uncle sows soybean every year."
opts: Soybean is sown every year by my uncle.
Soybean are sown every year by my uncle.
Soybean is sow every year by my uncle.
screens.ans: Soybean is sown every year by my uncle.

screens.ask: Make it active: "A horse is ridden by me." → "I ___ a horse."
screens.why: Active simple present with "I": base verb ride.

screens.text: "Spices are sown in between the onions and peppers." Why is there no "by…" phrase?
opts: The doer is not important, so it is left out
It is in the past tense
screens.ans: The doer is not important, so it is left out
screens.why: The active version is "We sow spices…"; in the passive, the doer "we" is dropped because it adds nothing.
screens.clue: Who sows them? Does it matter?

items.ask: Passive: "Fathers teach their sons and daughters about farming." → "Sons and daughters ___ about farming by their fathers."
Active: "The smallest income is earned by daily labourers." → "Daily labourers ___ the smallest income."

test.text: Which is the active form of "Milk is given by cows"?
